name: Home Team Energy Company
old_description: Milwaukee & Madison’s Trusted Solar Panel Installation Company
about:
Home Team Energy Company is a residential solar installer based in Brookfield, Wisconsin, serving the Milwaukee and Madison areas. Founded in 2019 by Ryan Lettau, a Milwaukee School of Engineering graduate with a decade of solar industry experience, the company began as a family operation run from a garage. Lettau's wife, Shelly, managed permitting and logistics while their young sons assisted with site cleanup, establishing a deliberately small, family-owned structure that remains central to the business.

The firm provides turnkey solar energy systems for homeowners across Southern Wisconsin, handling design, permitting, and installation with its own in-house crews rather than subcontractors. Services include rooftop solar arrays, battery storage, and EV charger installation. Since launch, the team has completed more than 700 residential projects comprising over 13,000 installed panels, with typical installations ranging from two days to four weeks from contract signing to commissioning.

Home Team Energy serves exclusively residential customers, primarily homeowners of WE Energies territory who want to offset rising electricity costs through net metering. The company does not pursue commercial or utility-scale work, focusing instead on single-family homes where the founder can still meet personally with each client.

Lettau started the company after watching rapid growth at a previous solar employer erode customer service. He designed Home Team Energy to stay "intentionally small" so that quality and direct communication never give way to volume. The firm emphasizes transparent pricing, honest advice on battery ROI, and full project management from permit to permission-to-operate.

name: Homestead Furniture
old_description: Homestead is furniture you experience, not scroll past. Made-to-order pieces. Real materials. Thoughtful design—guided by conversation, not a cart.
about:
Homestead Furniture operates from a three-floor showroom in Mt Hope, Ohio, where it has served customers for over 35 years. The company presents itself as a destination for custom furniture, emphasizing a consultative approach over transactional sales.

The business offers made-to-order hardwood and upholstered pieces, coordinating everything from hand-applied finishes to tailored dimensions. It carries multiple brands — including Abner Henry — and provides in-house design consultation, delivery, and assembly. The showroom spans curated residential and commercial vignettes, allowing clients to experience materials and scale in person.

Clients range from homeowners furnishing living rooms and dining areas to interior designers specifying custom pieces for commercial projects such as an optometric practice and a coffee shop. Homestead ships to all 50 states and 10 countries, though the bulk of its engagement appears to begin with an on-site or virtual design conversation.

The company frames customization as its founding principle rather than a recent add-on, positioning the design dialogue as the core of its process. Testimonials highlight bespoke items like a live-edge walnut bar sourced from a record-setting tree and a 108-inch dining table with pull-out leaves.

name: Hope & Main
old_description: Join us for a packed session designed to answer your biggest questions and help you take the first step to start or grow your food biz dreams!
about:
Hope & Main operates from Warren, Rhode Island, where it was founded in 2014 as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit culinary incubator. The organization emerged to address the high barriers food entrepreneurs face when launching products, offering shared commercial kitchen space and structured business support.

The incubator provides a tiered co-packing service alongside its flagship Warren kitchens, with a second location, West End Kitchens, slated to open in 2026. Since inception, the program has helped launch more than 550 food and beverage businesses, giving members access to production facilities without the capital expense of equipping and maintaining their own plants.

Clients are early-stage food and beverage entrepreneurs seeking to test, scale, or pivot products. The incubator serves makers across categories such as packaged foods, beverages, and specialty items, connecting them with educators, industry professionals, and a marketplace in Providence.

The organization states its mission is to empower an inclusive community of entrepreneurs to build a more just, sustainable, and resilient local food economy. It positions itself as an integrated resource system, a community of educators, and an advocacy voice for small food businesses.

name: Horizon Equipment
old_description: We partner with extraordinary restaurateurs to bring their vision to life.
about:
Horizon Equipment is based in Eagan, Minnesota, and serves the commercial foodservice industry with a focus on custom kitchen solutions. The company designs, equips, installs, and maintains commercial kitchens for a range of clients, from independent restaurants to large-scale commissary bakeries.

Its services cover the full project lifecycle: full kitchen and restaurant design, equipment procurement, CFESA-certified installation, equipment training, and ongoing maintenance. Technicians provide 24/7/365 field support for any equipment that stores, chills, freezes, prepares, cooks, holds, displays, or serves food. The firm does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volume.

Horizon works primarily with restaurateurs, chefs, brewers, and hospitality venues. A referenced project includes the Edina Country Club, where the general manager praised the company’s service throughout a remodel. The client base spans restaurants, breweries, country clubs, and other foodservice operations.

The company emphasizes a relationship-driven approach, stating it never uses templated proposals and tailors each kitchen to the client’s specific needs. Its principals highlight old-school, in-person relationships as a key differentiator in a technology-heavy market.

name: HornBlasters, Inc.
old_description: FOR A CHANCE AT $500 STORE CREDIT TELL US HOW YOU HEARD ABOUT US! / ORDER NOTES
about:
HornBlasters, Inc. is based in Tampa, Florida, and was founded in 2002 by owner Matt Heller. The idea originated during Heller's daily commute when he grew frustrated with being overlooked by other drivers. Drawing on a lifelong fascination with locomotive air horns, he began adapting that massive sound for everyday vehicles, initially operating out of his bedroom and selling kits from the back of his pickup truck before leaving his day job to grow the business full-time.

The company designs and assembles a wide range of air-horn and onboard-air products, including multi-chime train horn kits, standalone horns, spare-tire-delete mounting systems, 12- and 24-volt onboard air systems, compressors, air tanks, valves, fittings, pressure switches, and complete wiring kits. It also offers electric horns, marine horns, and public-address units, along with a library of instruction manuals, wiring diagrams, and an installer-locator service to support DIY and professional installation.

HornBlasters serves automotive enthusiasts, truck and SUV owners, commercial fleets requiring 24-volt systems, marine operators, and motorcycle riders. Its products are marketed to drivers seeking louder warning devices for safety, as well as to hobbyists building custom air-suspension or air-accessory setups. The installer locator connects customers with professional shops across the United States.

Heller has stated that the business was started to make roads safer by ensuring drivers are heard, turning a personal safety concern into a product line that now includes a two-year manufacturer's defect warranty on its branded kits.

name: Horst Sheet Metal Inc
old_description: Are you a designer, contractor or homeowner who desires a truly unique look or custom finish for your kitchen?
about:
Horst Sheet Metal Inc operates from New Holland, Pennsylvania, in Lancaster County. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure in its public materials, and no founders are named on its website.

The shop specializes in light-gauge custom metal fabrication, blending traditional handcrafted techniques with CNC machining and laser cutting. It produces kitchen accents such as stainless cabinet doors, copper sinks, backsplashes, range hoods, and countertops; roofing components including architectural moldings, ES-1 edgings, gutters, and downspouts; and HVAC parts like ductwork, fittings, adapters, wall caps, and piping. The facility also replicates historical moldings and finials for restoration projects. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

Customers include homeowners, contractors, kitchen manufacturers, designers, and architects. The company serves residential construction, commercial roofing, HVAC installation, historical restoration, and custom kitchen design sectors.

Horst Sheet Metal emphasizes its Lancaster County craftsmanship heritage, combining generational hand skills with modern automation. It markets environmentally friendly products made with a high percentage of recycled materials and promotes fast turnaround, attention to detail, and friendly service as operational differentiators.

name: Hubbell Incorporated
old_description: Manufactures electrical and utility solutions including switches, sockets, and panel board components.
about:
Hubbell Incorporated is headquartered in Shelton, Connecticut, and traces its origins to 1888. The company has operated continuously since its founding, evolving into a manufacturer of electrical and utility solutions for critical infrastructure.

The company produces a broad range of electrical components including switches, sockets, panel board parts, wiring devices, connection and control solutions, lighting and controls for harsh industrial environments, and datacom products for telecommunications and data centers. Its portfolio also covers utility and communications infrastructure solutions.

Hubbell serves diverse markets such as commercial construction, data centers, healthcare facilities, industrial manufacturing, original equipment manufacturers, fuels, power and utility, renewables, residential, water and gas distribution, and telecommunications. Customers include contractors, utilities, OEMs, and facility operators seeking reliable electrical infrastructure.

The company emphasizes solutions for critical infrastructure, integrating sustainability across its products and operations. It offers a competitor cross-reference tool to simplify part identification and has been recognized among the World's Most Ethical Companies. These elements reflect its focus on safety, reliability, and long-term performance.
